The National Hajj Commission of Nigeria has offered unsuccessful 2027 Hajj Savings Scheme subscribers the option of withdrawing their funds or retaining their savings in the scheme for the 2028 pilgrimage. NAHCON management, in a statement on Wednesday, also assured subscribers who fulfilled the payment requirements for the 2027 Hajj but could not secure slots that they would be given priority for the 2028 exercise, subject to approved quotas and regulatory requirements. The commission explained that the failure to accommodate all intending pilgrims was due to the global reduction in Hajj slots imposed by Saudi Arabian authorities because of space constraints. It stated, “The National Hajj Commission of Nigeria acknowledges the disappointment of Hajj Savings Scheme subscribers and, indeed, many Nigerian Muslims who fulfilled the financial requirements for the 2027 Hajj but could not secure slots, and appreciates their patience, sacrifices and commitment towards fulfilling this important religious obligation. “Nigeria, like other countries, is affected by the global reduction in Hajj slots imposed by the Saudi authorities due to space constraints. NAHCON is required to operate within approved quotas, regulations and timelines. “The Commission, however, welcomes the Saudi Government’s continued investment in Hajj infrastructure and remains hopeful that additional slots will become available in subsequent seasons.” NAHCON explained that the Hajj Savings Scheme allows intending pilgrims to save gradually while earning investment returns, stressing that full payment does not automatically guarantee a slot for a particular Hajj season. Retain their savings in the Scheme and continue to earn applicable investment returns, which may help offset future Hajj fares. “To strengthen allocation management, address existing backlogs and improve planning, NAHCON is developing a National Hajj Database in collaboration with State Muslim Pilgrims’ Welfare Boards, Agencies and Commissions, HSS partner banks and other relevant stakeholders.” NAHCON advised Hajj Savings Scheme subscribers and members of the public to seek information and guidance through its official channels and designated partner banks. The commission reaffirmed its commitment to ensuring equitable allocation of Hajj slots, transparency, compliance with regulations and the welfare of Nigerian pilgrims. Saudi Arabia approved an additional 10,000 slots for Nigeria on October 1, increasing the country’s 2027 Hajj quota from 50,000 to 60,000 pilgrims. However, despite the increase, some Nigerian intending pilgrims who made payments were unable to secure slots for the 2027 pilgrimage due to the limited allocation.
